new_statements.translation: Stress is dynamic and usually falls on the end of the word. In compound words a secondary stress arises: dàst-xålī́ 'empty-handed'. In verb forms the stress falls on the prefixes, on the negative particle, and in the past tenses it may fall on the stem. Unstressed are: the article -ī, the ezafe marker -e, the subject-object nominal marker -ā, and also the pronominal enclitics (enclitic pronouns) that mark person and number with transitive verbs in the past tenses. In connected speech phrasal stress, uniting certain syntactically bound groups of words, plays a substantial role.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is final (last syllable of the word) in nominals; clitic-like grammatical suffixes (indefinite article -ī, ezafe -e, nominal -ā, pronominal enclitics) do not take stress, so stress stays on the last syllable of the stem; in verbs stress shifts to preverbal prefixes (mī-/be-) and to the negative particle na-/ma-, and in past-tense forms may sit on the stem.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the first member of compounds (dàst-xålī́).
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed enclitics/suffixes (-ī, -e, -ā, pronominal clitics); verbal prefixes and negation attract stress (p. 186: Bur. ná-andä 'they did not come'); past-tense verbs may be stem-stressed; phrasal stress prominent in running speech.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the word; author adds that phrase-level stress groups syntactically bound words in connected speech. Data are for Somghuni, Papuni, Buringuni and Masarmi (villages near Kazerun), compiled from earlier field materials (Mann 1909 etc.), not the author's own fieldwork.
new_statements.identity_note: Kerimova's 'Farsa dialekty' describes the four village dialects Somghuni (somg1234), Papuni (papu1256), Buringuni (buri1259) and Masarmi (masa1326) near Kazerun -- all Glottolog dialects of sout2645 -- from earlier published materials (chiefly Mann 1909), not her own fieldwork. Davani (dava1250), treated separately by Moshkalo 1997 and Mahamedi 1994, has no stress statement in the sources opened. Behbahani, Angali, Kuhmara Sorkhi and Judeo-Shirazi varieties (also filed under sout2645 by Glottolog) are not covered by the quoted statement.
